source.notes: Fetched via the same doyenpublishers.com mirror pattern used for French/Science — WebFetch reported binary/unreadable content but saved the PDF locally, and Claude's Read tool parsed it natively. Structure verbatim from the PDF's SUMMARY OF STRANDS AND SUB STRANDS table and per-theme tables.

essenceNote: Kenya's foreign languages at Grade 9 are Arabic, French, German, and Mandarin — each a non-formal, basic (A1/YCT2-equivalent) 4-skills (listening, speaking, reading, writing) curriculum, taught in parallel structure across all four languages per the shared essence statement. German's design is structurally identical to French's: same 3 strands, same 9 themes in the same order.

notes: Same 9 themes repeat identically across all 3 strands, exactly mirroring French's structure. Each strand teaches the theme's vocabulary through a different modality (LS = oral vocabulary/expression recall, R = short German passage/dialogue + comprehension, W = spelling/gap-fill/word-order/functional writing). Per the standing 'never merge sub-strands' rule, this is 27 distinct skills (9 themes x 3 strands). Verbatim example phrases pulled directly from the curriculum design's own suggested-learning-experiences tables (marked 'z.B.' = 'zum Beispiel', for example) were used as the authentic vocabulary source for building skills, e.g. Ich heiße___/Ich bin___/Mein Name ist___ (greetings), Vater/Mutter/Bruder/Schwester/Oma/Opa (family), miaut-Katze/lange Nase-Elefant (animals), Ich stehe um 7 Uhr auf (routine), Ich möchte bitte...Darf ich...bestellen? (restaurant), Ich habe Kopfschmerzen/Ich gehe zum Arzt (health), Die Sonne scheint/Es regnet (weather), nach rechts/nach links/geradeaus (directions).
